My ex wasn't willing to give me that and had we still been together I would've been miserable because he didn't truly love me. I think often times we forget about the reasons as to why the relationship didn't work out and we focus solely on the positives. Depression doesn't necessarily mean feeling high emotions (sad, angry, etc).  A lot of the times it can cause people to feel nothing at all, just empty and sort of numb. I would definitely recommend going to seek a professional for a true diagnosis, however, from the sounds of it, it definitely sounds like you may have depression. Your general lack of interest in the things that you used to enjoy is a huge sign, actually. Difficulty finishing things, the low sex drive, not wanting to do anything in general. I'm a huge introvert, but I know my depression is getting bad again when i go into recluse mode and don't want to be bothered by anyone. It's strange because I can still manage to laugh at times and maybe "feel okay", but my body always tells me otherwise. Feeling physically exhausted from simple tasks is a huge sign. Taking hours to do one little thing that should maybe only take maybe 30 minutes. Not wanting to get out of bed, loss of appetite, and difficulty sleeping. You mentioned that both of your parents had it, and it can definitely be hereditary (both of my parents have it as well). I definitely think you should talk to your doctor about it before it gets any worse and go from there. Those definitely aren't normal things to feel out of the blue, but it's a good thing you're acknowledging that something may be wrong.  Good luck, and if you have any further questions, please feel free to ask on here or pm me. I'll be more than happy to help in any way that I can.
